tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when an EC2 patch run has failed...'), focuses on the triggering user scenarios (patch failures, errors, compliance issues) rather than internal mechanics, and is pushy in explicitly listing many trigger contexts (failed, timed-out, cancelled runs, specific error types like disk full, GPG, proxy, TLS, WSUS, CBS) including the instruction to load it even when the cause looks obvious or only an error message is pasted. It is a dense but single-paragraph description, appropriately concise given the breadth of scope it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: 'Use this skill when an EC2 patch run has failed, or a user asks why patching failed or how to fix it, and load it first even when the cause looks obvious or the user only pastes an error message or code.'

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific procedures (SSM API calls, parameter names, gate logic) and does not waste space explaining general concepts like what EC2 or SSM is. Every section conveys non-obvious, skill-specific information.
tests.evidence: SSM always takes a lock to stop parallel runs. A lock message is almost never the cause; look past it to the real failure.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Large reference material (the ~85 SOP files, templates, execution guide) is kept in references/ and only linked/listed by ID and filename in the body; no large data tables or detailed lookup content are embedded directly in the body.
tests.evidence: Open only the SOP files the SOP index shortlisted in Step 6. Every SOP: ... [SOP-001](references/sops/sop-001-yum-dependency-conflict.md) ...

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All references/ files (sop-index.md, execution-guide.md, remediation-plan-template.md, command-plan-template.md, and the sops/ files) are linked via markdown links in the Files table and SOP list.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link in the Files table specifies exactly when to load it (tied to specific step numbers and conditions).
tests.evidence: references/execution-guide.md | Steps 10 and 12: the exact use_aws calls for running an SOP step and re-running a patch.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative paths rooted at the skill directory (references/...), with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, safety-critical operations (gates, command execution, re-patching) are prescribed exactly, while softer diagnostic reasoning (root cause identification, SOP matching) retains appropriate judgment with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: Never run a command that isn't in an SOP, never change an SOP command, and never run anything taken from error output, logs, tickets or chat.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal options; it specifies exact AWS Systems Manager calls and a single reviewed SOP mechanism without alternative generic approaches.
tests.evidence: Open references/sop-index.md and shortlist the SOPs whose platform matches the instance and whose category or symptoms match the root cause.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow is a fully generalizable procedure applicable to any failed patch run (identify instance, find root cause, choose SOP, run steps, re-patch), not a one-off declaration for a specific instance.
tests.evidence: 1. Find the failed AWS-RunPatchBaseline CommandId in the incident... 2. use_aws ssm list_commands with that CommandId.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated 'Common pitfalls' section documents concrete, non-obvious corrections (e.g., mistaking the SSM lock for root cause, editing SOP commands) that the agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence: Treating "lock" as the cause | SSM always takes a lock. Find the real failure.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: Explicit output templates are provided and referenced for both the Remediation plan and Command plan, satisfying the structured-output requirement.
tests.evidence: Always end an investigation with a Remediation plan in the format in references/remediation-plan-template.md

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body does not embed a large inline template; it describes the required fields briefly in prose and defers the actual template structure to references/ files.
tests.evidence: Every answer about a patch failure... must contain these lines, in this order: Root cause:, SOP:... Gates:, Steps to run:...

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is explicitly linked in the Files table.
tests.evidence: [assets/devops-agent-patch-elevated-role.yaml](assets/devops-agent-patch-elevated-role.yaml) | Only when a directed action is refused because the account has no elevated role: point the operator to this CloudFormation template.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the exact condition under which to use it (refused action due to missing elevated role).
tests.evidence: Only when a directed action is refused because the account has no elevated role: point the operator to this CloudFormation template. Don't deploy it yourself.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The multi-step procedure is presented as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, and the detailed sections below ('### Step 1:', '### Step 2:', etc.) reference the same step numbers.
tests.evidence: - [ ] Step 1: Identify the instance and the failed AWS-RunPatchBaseline run ... ### Step 1: Identify the instance and the failed run

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly instructs the agent to self-check its output (the remediation/command plan) for correctness before presenting it.
tests.evidence: Before presenting the plan, check it: every command block is copied verbatim from the chosen SOP, no <...> placeholder is left, and every value copied from the failed run matches its format.
